land.text: Lower Nubia, ruled from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim after Dongola was lost in 1365

predecessors.note: The same kingdom: Cliopatria's 'Makuria' and 'Makuria Kingdom' rows share Wikidata Q829356 and the Makuria page treats them as one continuous state. The makuria dossier (af-01-a) hands over in 1414 as a hand-over, not a succession; one colour for both slugs.

land.text: the traditional view: 'conquered by the Funj Sultanate, founded in 1504' (Dotawo page)

successors.note: Traditional end only. The Makuria page has the Funj holding Dongola by 1523 and the Ottomans occupying Lower Nubia in the mid-16th century; the funj-sultanate dossier does not draw Lower Nubia.

land.text: Lower Nubia, occupied by the Ottomans

successors.note: Makuria page: the Ottomans 'finally conquered Nubia as far south as the 3rd cataract' in the mid-16th century and 'By the 1560s' Makuria 'had finally disappeared'.

capitals.name: Gebel Adda (Daw)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Dongola (5th century to 1365), then Gebel Adda (after 1365)'. The Dotawo page lists Daw as capital and says some scholars identify Daw with Gebel Adda; Qasr Ibrim was the second centre ('centered around the castles of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim'). Coordinates are the researcher's.

correction.text: Lower Nubia from the first to the second cataract, the Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim kingdom, clipped from Cliopatria's 1415 shape

keyframe_review.note: The shape (212,627 km2, 30.5-35.3 E, 17.9-23.8 N) runs from Aswan to south of Dongola. The Makuria page: after 1365 the kingdom 'lost much of its southern territories, including Dongola' and was 'centered around the castles of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim'; the 15th-century extent was 'at least from Qasr Ibrim in the north to Meinarti at the 2nd cataract', 'perhaps still extending as far north as the 1st cataract'; the Banu Kanz were expelled from Aswan in 1412/3. The correction clips the shape to Lower Nubia. The page gives no area (infobox area absent); 1415-1504 only.

correction.text: no Makurian state for 1507-1515; do not draw (stateless Nubian 'lords'); the outline is Cliopatria's and is not endorsed

keyframe_review.note: The shape (240,898 km2, now reaching 17.3 N) is larger than any extent after 1365 and is drawn for 1507-1515, after the kingdom's end. The Dotawo page: 'The end of Dotawo has traditionally been placed around the year 1500', 'conquered by the Funj Sultanate, founded in 1504' (a revised view has it surviving into the 17th century); the Makuria page: 'About the year 1500 ... no king but only lords', Dongola Funj by 1523, Lower Nubia Ottoman in the mid-16th century. The land belongs to no state in these years.

correction.text: no Makurian state for 1516-1518; do not draw

keyframe_review.note: As 1507, for 1516-1518. The Makuria page records only that 'an Egyptian source mentioned a Nubian ruler' in 1518 without saying where he lived or his religion; that does not make a kingdom.

region.text: Lower Nubia, the kingdom of Gebel Adda

ledger.note: 1415: the Makurian rump kingdom of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim, as Cliopatria begins its 'Makuria Kingdom' row. The pages date no event in 1415; this is the same kingdom as the makuria dossier. The last dated step before is 1412/3: 'The Banu Kanz were finally expelled from Aswan in 1412/3', so that Makuria 'lost the border to Egypt for good'.

1504: the traditional end of the kingdom. 'conquered by the Funj Sultanate, founded in 1504' (Dotawo page, traditional view); the Makuria page has the Funj holding Dongola by 1523 and the Ottomans in Lower Nubia in the mid-16th century, so the land passes to no state at once.

1504: the Nubian kingdom ends (traditional date). 'The end of Dotawo has traditionally been placed around the year 1500'; the Makuria page: Makuria 'most likely collapsed soon after the reign of Joel (attested 1463), probably still in the late 15th century' and 'About the year 1500' John reported 'no king but only lords'. The Dotawo page's revised view (Simmons) has it continuing 'into the seventeenth century'; Queen Gaua is dated to the 1520s.

certainty.note: No frontier is described on either page except the 'first cataract' guess and the Aswan border lost for good in 1412/3.

notes:
One kingdom in two Cliopatria rows. 'Makuria' (347..1414) and 'Makuria Kingdom' (1415..1518) share Wikidata Q829356 and Wikipedia title 'Makuria'; the pages describe one continuous kingdom, so the makuria dossier (af-01-a, earlier slug) already hands over to this slug in 1414 as the same state; the brief's 'one dossier under the earlier slug' cannot be applied because makuria belongs to part a. Both slugs should share one colour (rule 2). This dossier opens with a found event written as a hand-over.

Cliopatria problems: the 1415 shape reaches Dongola and south of it, which the page says was lost in 1365 (adjust: clipped to Lower Nubia); the 1507 and 1516 shapes (up to 240,898 km2) are drawn after the kingdom's end and are larger than any extent after 1365 (wrong). The end is 1504 on the traditional view (Dotawo page); the Makuria page puts the collapse 'probably still in the late 15th century' and the Dotawo page's revised view runs it into the 17th century (Queen Gaua in the 1520s); the 1518 Egyptian mention of a 'Nubian ruler' is undated in location. 1501/1504-1523 Lower Nubia is stateless (grey) until the Ottomans in the mid-16th century; the Dongola reach north of the Funj is Banu Kanz (no dossier yet, banu-kanz) then Funj by 1523 (Makuria page).

No rulers list (no complete list on the pages); no wars (none dated inside 1415-1504). Page budget: two pages (Makuria, Dotawo). Failed pages: none. Gazetteer names: 'Lower Nubia' exists; Gebel Adda coordinates are the researcher's (22.31 N, 31.62 E).
